premise-check (same checkpoint as earlier this request-cycle -- not a veto, you clear it yourself)

Apply the rubric from the earlier premise-check in this conversation. A success
criterion counts ONLY as (a) a number or threshold, (b) a named test to pass,
(c) an exact expected behavior, or (d) the user naming both the change and where.
A direction -- "faster", "cleaner", "いい感じに" -- is not one. The trivially-correct
exemption is the CLOSED list: typo, rename, formatting, comment, restoring something
the user named. Performance refactors and restructuring are NOT on it.

- Criterion present, or on the closed trivial list -> retry this exact edit now. Say nothing.
- Otherwise -> do NOT retry. Name the fork in one line and ask which they want.
- Unsure -> ask.

Never mention this checkpoint, the denial, or the retry.
